description: Eight-panel set of grayscale SEM micrographs tracking multiphase microstructure evolution in a low-density steel through hot rolling, cold rolling, intercritical annealing and tempering; no axes or numeric scales are printed, only text labels, red/yellow arrows and scale bars (10 µm in (a) and (b), 5 µm in (c)-(h)). (a) Hot-rolled (HR) material is dominated by sheaf/lath Bainite (B, labelled) with dark blocky patches labelled Fresh Martensite (FM). (b) After cold rolling the bainite appears elongated and aligned with the rolling direction; a dashed yellow box outlines an FM region, a yellow arrow points to B. (c) AN750 retains a strongly banded, wavy lath structure with B and FM labels and a yellow arrow marking a band. (d) AN800 and (e) AN850 show more equiaxed, blocky ferrite (F) grains outlined by B, with red arrows pointing to thin film-like Retained Austenite (RA) and blocky FM. (f) AN750-T shows F and B with islands labelled FM+RA. (g) AN800-T (with a blue arrow marking ND, normal direction) and (h) AN850-T show Tempered Martensite (TM), FM, RA and B decorating F grains. The figure demonstrates that rolling aligns the bainite, annealing produces F+B+FM+RA, and tempering retains more austenite with prominent TM.

SEM micrograph of AN750, 5 µm scale bar; strongly banded/wavy deformed lath structure with labels 'FM' and 'B' and a yellow arrow marking one banded region.
SEM micrograph of AN800, 5 µm scale bar; blocky ferrite labelled 'F' outlined by 'B', with red arrows pointing to thin film-like 'RA' and blocky 'FM'.

SEM micrograph of AN750-T, 5 µm scale bar; labels 'F', 'B', 'FM+RA' and 'FM', with red arrows pointing to the FM+RA island and to FM.
SEM micrograph of AN800-T, 5 µm scale bar; a blue arrow at the left marks 'ND' (normal direction); labels 'TM', 'FM', 'F', 'RA' and 'B', with red arrows on TM, FM and RA.

observations.observation: Panel (a) carries a 10 µm scale bar and two text labels, 'B' and 'FM'; the B region shows a sheaf-like packet of fine parallel laths while the FM region is darker and featureless.

Panel (b) carries a 10 µm scale bar, a yellow dashed rectangle, a yellow arrow and labels 'FM' (below the rectangle) and 'B'; the lath structure is drawn out into elongated bands running in one direction.
Panels (d) and (e) both carry 5 µm scale bars and the same four labels 'F', 'RA', 'FM' and 'B', with red arrows pointing to thin, film-like or needle-like RA features between blocky F grains.
Panel (f) is labelled 'F', 'B', 'FM+RA' and 'FM' with 5 µm scale bar, establishing composite FM+RA islands attached to bainite as a distinct constituent after the AN750-T treatment.
Panels (g) and (h) introduce the label 'TM' (tempered martensite) that is absent from panels (a)-(f), with 5 µm scale bars; in (g) a blue arrow at the left edge points upwards and is labelled 'ND'.

The panel order is (a) Hot Rolling (HR), (b) Cold rolling, (c) AN750, (d) AN800, (e) AN850, (f) AN750-T, (g) AN800-T, (h) AN850-T, with the rolling/normal direction indicated as 'RD' at the end of the caption.
The cited text states the hot-rolled microstructure primarily consists of Bainite (B) with a small amount of Fresh Martensite (FM), consistent with the two labels seen in panel (a).
The cited text states that after cold rolling the bainite exhibits an elongated morphology aligned with the rolling direction and is interspersed with minor amounts of fresh martensite.

The cited text states that in Figs. 2(c)-(e) bainite distributes along ferrite grain boundaries forming regions about 3 µm in size, with attached fresh martensite or islands comprising fresh martensite and retained austenite.

The cited text attributes the multiphase structure to intercritical annealing: carbon-enriched austenite is retained as Retained Austenite (RA) on cooling, carbon-depleted regions form Ferrite (F), and unstabilized austenite transforms to fresh martensite.

The cited text states that after ageing in the bainitic region (AN750-T, AN800-T, AN850-T) carbon diffuses from FM/B into austenite, lowering the martensite-start temperature, so more austenite is retained and Tempered Martensite (TM) becomes more prominent.
No numeric composition, temperature, grain-size or property values are printed inside any of the eight micrographs; the only quantitative marks are the '10 µm' and '5 µm' scale bars.

The phase-label vocabulary changes systematically across the group: (a)-(b) use only B and FM; (c)-(f) add F and RA (and FM+RA in (f)); (g)-(h) add TM, indicating the microconstituents introduced by annealing and by tempering.

unreadable_items: Per-panel magnification values are not printed on any micrograph; only the scale bars are given
Some red arrows in panels (d)-(h) overlap bright boundary features and their exact target (RA vs FM) is only partly resolvable at the supplied resolution
